title: Palindrome or not
prompt:
The starter reads one word of up to 63 letters into `word`. Finish it so it says whether the word is a palindrome: a word that reads the same forwards and backwards. Capitals count as the same letter as their lower-case twin, so `Racecar` is a palindrome.

Use two pointers. One starts on the first byte of `word`, the other on the last letter, which is the byte just before the terminating zero. Load a byte through each with `ldrb`, fold capitals to lower case, and compare. The first mismatch settles the answer; if the pointers meet or cross without one, the word is a palindrome.

In ASCII a capital sits exactly 32 below its lower-case letter, so adding 32 to any byte from `'A'` to `'Z'` folds it. Doing that twice per step is a good job for a small leaf subroutine.

Print the word as it was typed, followed by `is a palindrome` or `is not a palindrome`, using the two format strings in `.data`.

## what is checked

- the verdict for the word in the stdin box, and for more words you cannot see (so it has to work for any word)
- the program exits cleanly
- the letters are read one byte at a time (`ldrb`)
starter:
// read one word and report whether it reads the same both ways, ignoring case
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(left_r, x19)
define(right_r, x20)

.data
fmt_word:   .string "%63s"
fmt_yes:    .string "%s is a palindrome\n"
fmt_no:     .string "%s is not a palindrome\n"

.bss
word:       .skip 64                        // 63 letters plus the zero byte

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_word
        ldr     x1, =word
        bl      scanf

        // TODO: point left_r at the first letter and right_r at the last
        // one (the byte just before the zero). Walk them toward each
        // other one byte at a time, treating 'A' to 'Z' as 'a' to 'z'.
        // Stop at the first mismatch, or when the two pointers meet.
        // Then print the word with fmt_yes or fmt_no.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
